question: Why was the funding cash-and-carry idea (experiment E8.1) closed?
reference: All 8 runs failed (Binance ETH and BTC 2019 to 2026 and Hyperliquid 900 days, 30- and 90-day windows). Annualized funding was 10.8 to 13.9% a year, but the break-even was 9.6 to 13.7% because of round-trip costs, the idle 50% margin and the USDC benchmark, so win rates were only 17 to 56% and the last 180 days were negative everywhere. It worked only in 2020 and 2021; 2022 had 0% winning windows. The class was closed: not to be revisited without new data, at most as a signal if funding stays above 20% a year for weeks.

question: Why was providing liquidity on Aerodrome rejected for the wide cbBTC/WETH position (experiment E8.4)?
reference: A position staked in an Aerodrome gauge earns only AERO emissions and no fees, and the displayed emission APR is computed on liquidity in the active tick plus or minus one tick (about a 0.3% band). A ±40% position has about 6.5 units of liquidity per dollar against about 1 300 for the narrow band, so it would get about 0.5% of the emissions, roughly 4 to 6% a year in AERO (an inflating token), against roughly 5 to 11% a year in fees on Uniswap. The Aerodrome advantage exists only for ultra-narrow, actively managed positions, the class already falsified in late August. Verdict: no, Uniswap stays the venue for the wide position; closed for good.

question: What happened in the .bot and pipeline incident of 17 August, and how was it resolved?
reference: The bot state directory .bot was tracked in git while the Windows auto-pull runner did a git reset --hard every 3 minutes, which would overwrite live data. CC-Win backed up the data (robocopy) and stopped the runner, then found that the HomosPipeline task ran as SYSTEM and failed with spawn npx ENOENT, and moved it to the user account; CC-Mac untracked .bot (commit f18f50e) only after the backup was confirmed; CC-Win pulled, restored the backup and restarted the runner and the bot. No data was lost. (The next day the auto-pull runner was withdrawn altogether.)

question: Why was @envio-dev/hypersync-client pinned to exactly version 1.0.0?
reference: On 19 Aug: Envio ships no Windows (win32) binary after 1.0.0. The caret range resolved, on Windows, to a wrapper without the native module, while it worked on macOS. The API used is identical in 1.0.0, so the dependency was pinned to exactly 1.0.0 across the repository.

question: What exit rule for the tranche was set on 2 September, and how did the revision of 16 September change it?
reference: 2 Sep: exit the LP on 24 Sep regardless of price, earlier if the tranche balance reaches +5%; manual daily monitoring, deliberately no automation (the product beat HODL in none of five measurements). 16 Sep, the day after a 4% drop: exit the LP when the tranche balance is at or above the deposit (0%); the hard 24 Sep exit and the +5% trigger are dropped; 24 Sep becomes a review; a balance at or below -10% forces a new decision; the bet is reviewed on 24 Oct; still no narrowing. The loss was market beta (about -$12 against HODL) and the owner kept a conscious bet on an ETH/BTC recovery.

question: What did ALGORITHM v1, frozen on 11 August, specify, and what evidence was it based on?
reference: k = 3 for ETH/stable pairs and k = 2 for cbBTC, a 24-hour hysteresis, a payback limit of 7 days, and a trend breaker that simply exits on a 5% break below the 7-day EMA. Evidence: a 365-day walk-forward plus 5 out-of-sample cross-validation runs; the exit profile was the best outside the tuning pool and had the fewest parameters.

question: On 26 August the validation gate moved to a 720-day window because no configuration passed on 720 days. In the saved 720-day walk-forward results for Base WETH/USDC 0.30%, Base cbBTC/WETH 0.05%, mainnet USDC/WETH 0.05% and Arbitrum WETH/USDC 0.05%, did passive ±50% meet the soundness criterion (win rate at least 65% and worst window above -3%) or the two-regime gate on any of them?
reference: No. With 30-day windows every 15 days (47 or 48 windows): Base WETH/USDC 0.30% win rate 59.6%, worst -11.7%; Base cbBTC/WETH 0.05% 63.8%, worst -7.76%; mainnet USDC/WETH 0.05% 60.4%, worst -11.8%; Arbitrum WETH/USDC 0.05% 66.0%, worst -12.0% (the win rate passes, the worst window fails). On every pool the mean against HODL is positive only in the flat regime (up and down are negative), so the two-regime gate fails too. The decision log records 0 of 21 configurations passing on 720 days.
notes: Needs at least 4 result reads plus a source for the gate; a stress test of the step limit.

question: In experiment E8.2 the journal reports that GM-BTC/USD passed all four house-edge criteria. What numbers did the journal report, and do the numbers in the saved result file match them?
reference: Journal, 7 Sep (GM v2, Sep 2023 to Sep 2026, 90-day windows every 30 days, n = 33, against HODL 50% BTC / 50% USDC): mean +2.30% per window, win rate 91%, worst -1.65%, positive edge in 3 of 3 regimes, max drawdown 26.1% against 41.8% for the basket, so 4 of 4 criteria. Saved file e8-house-GM-BTC-USD-btc50-90d: mean +2.35%, win rate 93.9%, worst -1.68%, positive in all three regimes (up +2.19, down +1.58, flat +3.33), drawdown 25.9% against 41.6%. Close but not identical; the journal records later fixes of the price data (E8.2e, E8.2f on 9 Sep) that moved the numbers slightly. The verdict, 4 of 4, is the same.
notes: The four criteria themselves are listed in the legend (from vault-house-edge.ts), not in the journal entry.
